fed.probabilities_note: Market-implied Fed path, read from the curve instead of the licensed CME futures feed: the gap between the 1-year Treasury and the current target midpoint. Positive = easing priced, negative = tightening priced. A real signal, not an option-implied probability.
fed.caveat: The Fed does not set mortgage rates. It moves the front end; mortgage rates follow the 10Y and the MBS spread.

bullets.text: 10-year Treasury at 4.92%, -12 bp on the day. This is the single biggest input to your rate.
Published 30-year survey at 7.28%, +17 bp week over week. It is a weekly average and always lags your rate sheet.
Mortgage spread 224 bp, normal at the 61th percentile of 10 years. That is 2.24 points of the 7.28% rate coming from spread, not from Treasuries.
10-Year Treasury -12 bp, bigger than 96% of moves on record. Expect rate sheets to follow.

why.headline: Mortgage rates are improving. The 10-year Treasury is 4.92% (-12 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.17%.
why.summary: The 10-year Treasury is at 4.92%, -12 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved +17 bp. That breaks down exactly: -6 bp from Treasuries and +23 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 224 bp, which is normal and sits at the 61th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly 16 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.

legs.chain: Brent crude (global benchmark) → ↑ Recession risk → ↓ 10Y Treasury → ↓ MBS yield → ↓ 30Y mortgage rate
legs.rationale: A sustained crude spike is a tax on the consumer. This is the offsetting channel: the same oil move that lifts inflation expectations also raises recession risk, and those two push mortgage rates in opposite directions.

brief.title: MORTGAGE MARKET MORNING BRIEF
brief.body: Mortgage rates: 7.28% published 2026-11-19, modeled 7.17% today. 10-year Treasury: 4.92% (-12 bp). MBS: 16.10 ticks. Rate bias: Improving. The mortgage spread is 224 bp, normal versus its 208 bp long-run average. Ahead: Core PCE Price Index on 11-28. Biggest risk: Core PCE Price Index. A hot print reverses any Treasury rally. What LOs should know: pull your float list and re-price. Improvements reach rate sheets with a one to two day lag
